gap_or_question: No decision exists on where the five named campaigns' targeting/decision logic is actually built: natively within MCP Personalization's own Experience/Decision framework (consuming activated Data 360 segments as inputs), or constructed as Data 360 Audience/Segment Flows that drive the activation itself. The discovery material names 'Marketing Cloud Personalization' as the activation target but never specifies the division of logic between the two platforms.
impact_or_notes: Two legitimate, documented-but-unreconciled patterns exist in the central KB: [KA-19954] (Selecting an Audience Source for Audience Flows, official) describes Data 360-side audience/segment flow construction, while [KA-23715]/[KA-23611] (Connect Data 360 to Marketing Cloud Personalization / Create MCP Data Streams in Data Cloud, official) describe dataset/segment hand-off into MCP where MCP's own targeting rules take over. Which pattern wins — or what splits where — changes which track (MCP Next vs. Data 360) owns the bulk of the build effort for each of the five campaigns, a real staffing-allocation question given the two-track staffing draft.

gap_or_question: Web campaign #2 serves higher-priced items to customers inferred (via Acxiom third-party data, not self-disclosed) to have higher household income. This is a personalized-pricing/merchandising practice driven by inferred demographic data, not just a data-privacy question about holding the income attribute.
impact_or_notes: 🔴 Ungrounded — distinct from G0002 (which covers compliance exposure on holding/processing the sensitive Acxiom attributes themselves). This gap is about the downstream pricing-practice exposure: several U.S. states have enacted or proposed personalized-pricing disclosure requirements, and algorithmic price differentiation by inferred income carries reputational and regulatory risk independent of the underlying PII handling. No atom in the central KB addresses retail personalized-pricing legal exposure (searches returned only Financial Services lending-eligibility content, not applicable here). [assumption: recommend Beyond's legal/compliance function review this specific use case — showing different price points to different customers based on inferred income — before design locks, separately from the general Acxiom compliance question already in G0002].

gap_or_question: Is user experience and content design effort — creative copy, imagery, responsive layout, and accessibility compliance (e.g., screen-reader behavior, focus management, color contrast) for dynamically-injected personalization overlays — included in this engagement's scope for the 10 web use cases and 5 named campaigns across 3 brand surfaces? impact_or_notes: Discipline gap (experience design signal), buyer-facing question. Distinct from G0106 (which asks who owns ongoing creative/content governance for the MCP Next track generally) — this is scoped specifically to build-time production effort and a technical accessibility risk particular to JS-injected content: client-side-injected overlays (mortgage ad, product-rec carousel, mover/back-to-college/patio creative) are commonly missed in standard accessibility audits because they don't exist in the page's initial DOM. If Beyond has an ADA/WCAG 2.1 AA compliance standard, injected personalization content needs to be tested against it explicitly, not assumed covered by whatever audit covers the static page.

gap_or_question: No success-measurement framework (click-through rate, conversion lift, revenue attribution per campaign) is defined for the five named web campaigns. Is a reporting/dashboard build — via MCP's own reporting, Data 360 analytics, or another tool — in scope to measure campaign performance, or is that entirely client-owned post-launch?
impact_or_notes: Without an agreed measurement approach, there's no way to validate whether any of the five campaigns actually achieved their stated business intent (e.g., mortgage-interest conversion, mover-targeting expansion) after go-live, and 'done' for this epic has no observable definition. Worth resolving alongside the governance question in G0107 (who owns ongoing campaign operations) since measurement ownership and operational ownership are usually the same conversation with the client.

gap_or_question: Pinterest and TikTok — both named in the epic description — have ambiguous connector/activation-target status within the client's own knowledge base. Three different sections name three different platform sets: the migration guide's 'platforms supported for activation' list (Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, Amazon Ads, SnapChat) omits both [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:11160-11164]; the AppExchange-vs-strategic-partner tier list (Liveramp/Criteo/Tradedesk vs. Google/LinkedIn/Meta/Amazon Ads) also omits both [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:124613-124619]; yet the Match Count feature's supported-advertising-platforms list includes both alongside Amazon, Meta, Google Ads, Google Ad Manager, Google DV360, LinkedIn, and Snapchat [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:130229-130237].
impact_or_notes: 🔴 Ungrounded on which connector tier (native External Activation Target, AppExchange partner, or something else) actually applies to Pinterest and TikTok. I ran the central-KB search (doc_search, kb-salesforce-prod) across multiple query variants and found no atom confirming Pinterest/TikTok's Data 360 connector classification — results surfaced only general Data 360 integration-pattern taxonomy (KA-0031, KA-5871) and Media Cloud ASM atoms, neither of which names these two platforms. Appearing in a reporting feature's supported-platform list doesn't confirm they're available as a build-able Activation target — match-count reporting could post-date, or be broader than, actual activation-target availability. Needs direct confirmation (Salesforce product docs or a live org check) before Pinterest/TikTok are staffed as same-effort builds alongside Google Ads/Facebook.

gap_or_question: Criteo activates through a materially different connector tier than Google Ads and Facebook (Meta): Criteo is grouped with Liveramp and Tradedesk as an 'AppExchange partner' integration, while Google, LinkedIn, Meta, and Amazon Ads are 'strategic partner' (native External Activation Target) integrations [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:124613-124619, confirmed by the glossary definition of External Activation Target at lines 2802-2808]. These are not interchangeable build patterns — the AppExchange tier requires installing and configuring a third-party-published package rather than using Data 360's native strategic-partner activation-target setup flow.
impact_or_notes: This resolves the epic's own kb_sources flag ('assumption: ad-platform activation connector pattern — not read against a specific Data 360 connector atom') with real grounding, sourced from the project's own layer-1 knowledge base per the sourcing-chain's stated priority (project knowledge/ wins when it directly answers the question). I also ran central-KB doc_search for a supporting atom; the closest hits were KA-0031/KA-5871 (Data 360 Integration Patterns Taxonomy / Pattern Selection Guide), which name 'Segment Activation to Marketing and Advertising Platforms' as a general asynchronous data-integration pattern but don't break out the AppExchange-vs-strategic-partner distinction at the per-platform level — so the central KB adds context, not the grounding itself. Sizing/estimating Criteo as equivalent effort to Google Ads or Facebook risks under-scoping a package-install-and-configure step the other two platforms don't need.

gap_or_question: Every External Activation Target in Data 360 requires a CPRA privacy-type designation (CPRA Third-Party, CPRA Service Provider, or Not Applicable) set at configuration time, used to indicate how CPRA (California Privacy Rights Act) applies to data shared with that platform [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:124572-124580]. Who at Beyond is the named decision-maker for classifying each of the five ad-platform activation targets (Google Ads, Facebook, Criteo, Pinterest, TikTok) under this designation, and on what basis?
impact_or_notes: Discipline gap (data-sharing governance signal) — buyer-facing question, not a mandated epic. This sits directly on top of the sensitivity already flagged project-wide in G0002: the Acxiom attribute set includes income, marital status, children-in-household, and home value, several of which feed the very segment types (expectant-family, college-affiliated) this epic activates to five external ad platforms. Getting the CPRA classification wrong on even one target is a compliance-facing configuration error with no technical safeguard preventing it — this needs a named owner before build, not left to whoever happens to click through setup.

gap_or_question: The epic's segment types mix in several sensitive-adjacent categories sourced from the Acxiom enrichment set — expectant-family, college-affiliated (aged or parent of), and arguably new-movers draw on attributes like household composition, children-in-household, and move date. Major ad platforms (Google, Meta in particular) maintain advertiser policies that restrict or prohibit using sensitive personal categories (health status/pregnancy, family/parental status) as direct ad-targeting or audience-definition criteria. Has anyone validated the six named segment definitions against each of the five target platforms' advertiser policies before these are built as activation segments?
impact_or_notes: Builds on G0002 (compliance/privacy posture, project-level) and G0306 (Acxiom license/usage-rights for paid-media activation) without duplicating either — this is a narrower, platform-policy-specific risk: a violation here risks ad-account suspension or audience rejection by the platform itself, not just a regulatory exposure. Should be checked per-platform (not just per-attribute) before segment-build work starts, since policy enforcement varies by platform and by exact targeting mechanism used (e.g., Customer Match upload vs. interest-category targeting).

gap_or_question: G0307 (project-level) already flags that the DMA-suppression attribute's enforcement mechanism is undefined — automatic exclusion filter vs. manual campaign-builder step. For paid-media activation specifically, this gap is more consequential than for web/email: once an ad has served an impression to a suppressed individual, there is no recall mechanism analogous to an unsent email. No stated design confirms the DMA-suppression field is wired as an automatic Activation Membership filter across all five of this epic's ad-platform activations.
impact_or_notes: Narrower, higher-stakes sub-gap of G0307 scoped specifically to this epic. If suppression enforcement is left to manual campaign-builder discipline rather than built into the Activation Membership filter architecture (Data 360 supports this per [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:124643-124660], 'Add Filters to Contact Points in Activation' / 'Add Filters to the Activation Membership'), a single missed step produces an irreversible compliance exposure across any of the five platforms. Recommend building this as a default-on filter at the activation-target level, not a per-campaign checklist item.

gap_or_question: Several of the six named segment types (college-affiliated, expectant-family in particular) are inherently narrow audiences. Google's own audience-insights feature requires a minimum of 1,000 activated members before it will generate a report [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:129748-129752], and ad-platform matching generally degrades — lower match rate, reduced campaign eligibility — below a platform-specific minimum audience size. No segment-size estimate exists for any of the six segment types across the three in-scope brands (BBY US, Overstock, BuyBuyBaby) to confirm activation viability on any of the five platforms.
impact_or_notes: This is the architecture/sizing counterpart to the already-logged open client question G0006 ('how many target segments are required per paid channel') — G0006 asks about segment count, this gap asks whether the segments as defined will actually be large enough to activate effectively once built. If some segment-brand combinations (e.g., BuyBuyBaby college-affiliated) fall below viable size, that's wasted build effort unless caught before segment design locks.

gap_or_question: Discipline gap (governance signal), buyer-facing question: this epic activates up to six segment types across five ad platforms across three brands — as many as 90 segment-platform-brand combinations at full build-out. Who on Beyond's side owns ongoing audience refresh cadence, match-rate monitoring, and retiring underperforming segments once this goes live?
impact_or_notes: Narrower than the project-level governance gaps already logged (G0004: broad MCP/Data 360 operating model; G0107: MCP Next-specific campaign governance) — scoped specifically to paid-media activation operations, which has its own cadence and failure modes (match-rate decay, platform policy changes, segment staleness) distinct from on-site personalization governance. Worth a dedicated line in the client question list rather than folding silently into the broader governance ask.

gap_or_question: Data 360's own guidance for optimizing ad-platform match rates recommends supplying all available match keys (email, phone, address, etc.) per profile and properly formatting consent values per the receiving platform's requirements [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:130250-130257]. No field-mapping or consent-value-formatting work has been scoped between Data 360's Unified Individual / Contact Point Digital ID fields and each of the five platforms' specific identifier requirements (e.g., Google Ads' accepted hashed-identifier set differs from Meta's and from Criteo's AppExchange-partner identifier model).
impact_or_notes: This is real, as-yet-unscoped build work — distinct from G0206 (identity resolution across brands) and from the activation-target setup itself. Without this mapping exercise, match rates on go-live are unpredictable and the per-platform configuration effort can't be sized accurately. Should be scoped per platform, not assumed to be a single generic mapping step.

gap_or_question: Data 360 activations support two refresh types — full (updates all records every run) or incremental (publishes only added/updated/deleted records since the last successful refresh) [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:123708-123714]. No refresh-type or cadence decision has been made for any of the six segment types across the five ad platforms. A recurring behavioral segment (seasonal/category purchasers) plausibly wants frequent incremental refresh; a slower-changing segment (new movers, college-affiliated) plausibly wants a different cadence — but nothing in the source material states this per segment type.
impact_or_notes: Affects both build scoping (incremental refresh has different setup/testing considerations than full refresh) and ongoing data-platform cost (refresh frequency drives credit consumption, per the project-level credit-sizing gap G0208 at the Data 360 foundation epic). Needs a cadence decision per segment type before activation builds are finalized.

gap_or_question: E04 lists 'near-real-time event-based messaging' as one of five MCP activation sub-types, but Data 360 reaches Marketing Cloud Personalization only through Segment Activation (an async, scheduled-publish mechanism — standard cadence 12 or 24 hours [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:118412-118629]), not through Data Action Targets, which are the platform's actual synchronous/near-real-time alerting mechanism. The supported Data Action Target list is explicitly Salesforce Platform Event, Webhook, and Marketing Cloud Engagement only [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:135711-135722] — MCP does not appear anywhere in that list (confirmed via full-document search, zero matches for 'Personalization' + 'data action' co-occurring). Real-Time Segments exist but carry hard restrictions (no exclusion criteria, no nested batch segments, no segment counts, no manual publish) and don't close this gap on their own.
impact_or_notes: Architecture-shaped fork grounded in the central KB: [KA-5871] ('Pattern Selection Guide for Data 360 Integrations') draws exactly this line — Asynchronous / Segment Activation to Marketing and Advertising Platforms vs. Synchronous / Real-Time Data Action for turning customer signals into instant action — and MCP sits only on the async side of that matrix. If 'near-real-time' is a literal client requirement (not just directional language), the near-real-time behavior will have to come from MCP's own native event/decisioning layer (ingested via the MCP connector) rather than from a Data 360 Data Action pushed into MCP. This changes where E04's near-real-time logic is built and should be resolved before design locks — left unresolved, the team risks committing to a Data 360-side near-real-time activation path that doesn't exist for this target.

gap_or_question: E04's 'cross-entity purchase/browse signal activation' (brand/entity A's signal activating a journey for entity B) is in tension with Data 360's standard multi-brand pattern of one Data Space per brand/location tenant [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:30310-30338, 34263-34399]. Data Spaces are documented as having hard isolation: you can't share data, content, campaigns, or access controls between data spaces.
impact_or_notes: Architecture-shaped fork, grounded: [KA-2766] ('Business Units in Marketing Cloud Next — Data Partitioning and Governance') and [KA-24122] ('Marketing Cloud Next Business Units built on Data Spaces') both state verbatim that data spaces have high walls and name 'You expect to share the same data space across multiple business units' as an explicit non-supported case. Reaching across BBY US / Overstock / BuyBuyBaby for signal activation therefore requires either (a) a shared/default data space spanning the three in-scope brands rather than per-brand isolation, or (b) explicit Data Share (zero-copy, object-level cross-space/cross-org sharing per [KA-0016]) configured for exactly the DMOs backing this signal. Neither option is named in the discovery material. This decision gates E04's cross-entity sub-type and should be made before data-space topology is finalized in the Data 360 track — it is also upstream of G0102 (identity-mapping owner at the MCP↔Data 360 seam), since cross-entity activation assumes a resolvable shared identity across whatever data-space boundary is chosen.

gap_or_question: E04's value segmentation and lifecycle targeting sub-types both depend on Calculated Insights, which in turn depend on identity resolution being settled first — but identity resolution strategy across the three brand domains is still open (existing gap G0206) and the Data Space/cross-entity decision (G0402) is also unresolved. No sequencing or dependency plan exists tying these three decisions together before E04's segmentation logic can be built.
impact_or_notes: If identity resolution (G0206) and data-space topology (G0402) aren't settled first, value/lifecycle segment definitions built against Calculated Insights will need to be rebuilt once the underlying unified-profile grain changes. This is a sequencing risk specific to E04, distinct from G0206/G0303 themselves (which are about the resolution strategy, not the build order) — recommend this be called out explicitly in the Data 360 track's work-breakdown so segmentation stories aren't started before the identity-resolution and data-space decisions land.

gap_or_question: The discovery material names E04's five activation sub-types (near-real-time event messaging, scheduled segment audiences, cross-entity signals, value segmentation, lifecycle targeting) but doesn't specify the actual trigger events or lifecycle milestones behind two of them: what specific user events qualify as 'near-real-time' triggers, and what specific lifecycle stages ('based on account create, last purchase, etc.' — the 'etc.' is undefined) should drive lifecycle targeting.

This is a buyer-facing question that should go back to Beyond alongside the existing open-questions list in the discovery brief (end users/personas, compliance, migration, governance, BigQuery schema, paid-media volume) — it's the same class of 'specifics deferred to a client question list' gap, scoped to E04 specifically.

gap_or_question: No stewardship or governance model is named for who owns segment and audience *definitions* once E04 is live — who can create, modify, or retire a value-segment or lifecycle-segment definition in Data 360, and who arbitrates when a segment's criteria conflict across the near-real-time, scheduled, and cross-entity activation paths.

Flag as a buyer-facing question for the client question list: who on Beyond's side owns ongoing segment/audience governance after go-live, and is there a change-control process for segment definitions that feed paid media as well as MCP?

gap_or_question: The Marketing Cloud Personalization connector ingests user profile and behavioral event data only from the point of connection creation onward — it does not backfill historical MCP engagement data for existing profiles [KB: data_360_4-10-2026.md:45422-45426]. impact_or_notes: At go-live, cross-entity and lifecycle segments built on Data 360-side MCP engagement data will only reflect activity from the connector's activation date forward, not Beyond's full MCP history (which has been live at BBY US and Overstock already — see current-state description). This creates a cold-start period where lifecycle/cross-entity targeting may under-perform or misfire until sufficient new-signal volume accrues. Recommend flagging this explicitly in the Data 360 track's cutover plan and considering whether a one-time historical export/backfill (outside the native connector) is needed — related to, but distinct from, the open data-migration question (G0003) which is scoped to MCP Next configuration, not Data 360 engagement history.
